thread.title: Apple: Buying Into The Sell-Off - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)

author: D. H. Taylor
title: Apple: Buying Into The Sell-Off - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)
text:
Apple's ( AAPL ) growth machine, the iPhone, has stalled in year-over-year change. Despite that, revenue and earnings for the past quarter are still increasing, albeit at a lower rate. I don't see this as the death knell for Apple. However, the stock is down sharply over the past few weeks. it was the price of their stock, bid up by overzealous investors, that was misaligned from the company's fundamentals. I believe Apple will continue to perform well and the recent selling has presented the market with a significantly reduced price to purchase the stock.
Here is a look at Apple's share price over the past few years:
First, Apple's stock may have been bid up along with the other FAANG stocks, Facebook ( FB ), Amazon ( AMZN ), Netflix ( NFLX ), and Google ( GOOG ) (NASDAQ: GOOGL ). And, subsequently, Apple's stock became equally overvalued in the hype. Now, the stock is coming back down to be more in line with the company's fundamentals.
Apple's stock price peaked at $233.00 the first week of October. It is now down to $172.00, a 26% drop. If the stock were to drop significantly more, this would bring the price in line with historic average PE ratios, as this chart shows:
Chart Source: Macrotrends
Future earnings for the company are expected to be $13.41 over the next year, whereas TTM comes in about $11.58 per share.
Over the past two years, the PE ratio was above average, peaking at about 20-times TTM. But, it has held roughly around 12.5-times over the longer period of time.
If you took a reasonable valuation of 12.5-times earnings, about what Apple averages for its TTM earnings, that comes in at $144.26 stock price; a price that is not that far off. This is actually my target for buying, a target I feel the market will hit over the next two weeks.
Some may question my price target; I am very used to that. I find those individuals are basing their analysis on hope, a dirty four letter word. I find the more successful investing style is plain fact-based numbers. And, I also find that enough patience rewards me; this target price will get hit.
When you look at revenue and earnings growth over the past several quarters, you start to question the wisdom in the marginal buyers that pushed Apple shares up to the highs of 20-times earnings as they did. Look at that last surge, and look at the earnings and revenue. Where does the justification come from? Where in Apple's fundamentals did it say that there is now going to be a such a tremendous increase in revenues and earnings to drive the price up like that, up to 20-times earnings? You have to wonder who the remaining marginal buyers were. And, now that the market has sunk as sharply as it has, putting the move into question is more easily answered.
The surge occurred on what I like to reference as being irrational exuberance, based upon the book of the same title. There was no fundamental rationale to push the price upwards to excessively high valuations. While I believe the stock will fall more, I see this as a solid opportunity to own a solid-performing stock.
There are other things about the business of Apple that are important to point out, such as what exactly does Apple sell?
iPhone sales It is all about the iPhone and its sales, correct? That is not entirely true. That is but one aspect of the company's business. Here is a breakdown of sales of products over the past few years from iPhones, iPads and iPods (a now forgotten species):
Source: Statista from Apple data
As you can see, iPhone sales are important to the company. But, iPad sales are slightly more important. They account for more sales overall. This is the trend of the company. Computers are going the way of the iPod; they are becoming a much smaller and smaller segment of the business. That trend portends what is about to happen within the company. Apple is trying to be far more than just the supplier of devices. Apple wants to be more of a service company. The devices are what they provide and then they want to be able to sell services brought to you on those devices. Sales of services continue to expand:
Apple Source Data via Staista
With over 2 billion iOS devices in the world, this is a strong platform to continue growing the services division of Apple. Services earned $10 billion in the fourth quarter, up from $7.9 billion the quarter before. Analyst expectations are that Apple's services segment will account for 25% of revenue in 2020, up from the current 16% in 2018 . Although growth in iPhones has slowed, services is what to be looking for in the future for Apple.
I am a diehard Apple product user. I bought my first Apple computer in 1986 and have never even considered the idea of owning anything else ever since. I have a MacBook Pro, iPad mini (becoming an extinct species) and an iPhone; the latter two needing to be upgraded in the next year. Just this morning, the services division got a whopping $0.99 out of me for the initial monthly installment of my never-ending marriage with the company: I upgraded my iCloud storage from the initial free 5Gb to 50Gb of storage. And, that is how they get you.
And that is how the company will continue to grow their services business. They have 2 billion iOS devices out there that they provide certain services for free. You find them useful. You use them. You upgrade the levels of service. And you contribute to Apple's top line and bottom line... both of which are continually moving higher.
Profits and growth The headline on the latest earnings release says it all: Everything was up .
"Revenue Up 20 Percent and EPS Up 41 Percent to New September Quarter Records. Services Revenue of $10 Billion Reaches New All-Time High"
Here is a visual to keep this in perspective:
Chart Source: Macrotrends
The company's revenue continues to move upward as this graphic shows. They had $62.9 billion in revenue for the quarter , up a stellar 20% (year-over-year) and earnings up 41%.
I believe iPhone and iPad sales are still going to be strong in the future for Apple. But, it is the services division that I will be continually keeping an eye on as that growth is where the company, and myself, see the future for Apple.
The Trade War While Apple's products have remained contained and have not been a target of the trade war, this is something that in the back of a lot of investors' minds is concerning. There have been calls that the economy is going to slow down in the coming year. This is not a view I fully embrace given the economic landscape we are in at this time. But, the trade war does have the ability to slow the economy and slow down sales at Apple . iPhone sales have stagnated as has already been pointed out. If the trade war gets pushed further, this will weigh on iPhone sales even more.
Takeaway I am waiting for the dust to finally settle from all of the selling that has occurred in the FAANG stocks. I would be a buyer of Apple at lower prices, based upon future earnings and the PE ratio that would come from an even more discounted share price. And, I would be a long-term holder of the stock. Right now, the PE ratio is more in line with long-term fundamentals and historical ratios. I would bet that we are getting close to the bottom of the selling in all of the FAANG stocks. Once the dust settles, I think it will be a good time to get back into the stock with a long.
I have been looking for an entry point into Apple's stock that I may buy-and-hold for many years. I do not have a specific target price, but instead a long-term outlook based upon a time frame, that being a retirement date (in about 15 years). After my entry point, I am expecting to see a reasonable return from the company over many years to come, and I believe the services segment will be the growth of that.
Disclosure: I/we have no positions in any stocks mentioned, but may initiate a long position in AAPL over the next 72 hours.
